parameters.content:
## Community engagement sync

An extension, not part of the core loop.

When HubSpot Community emails you that someone replied on a thread you
are in, Scout finds the matching Notion row and marks it as a live
conversation. If there is no matching row, it creates a hot one so the
new person does not fall through.

Scout reads your notification mail. It does not read your inbox at
large, and it does not reply to anything.

nodes.name: Test this before you activate it

parameters.content:
## Test this before you activate it

**Notification formats change.** The parser looks for a community topic
link inside whichever body field Gmail exposes. HubSpot can change that
template at any time, and when it does this extension quietly stops
matching.

Forward yourself a real community notification and run this workflow
manually against it **before** you activate it. Confirm that
**Parse Notification** produces a topic URL and a display name.

Messages without a community topic link are dropped on purpose.

## What Scout stores

Only the public display name shown in the notification and the topic
URL.

Nothing else from the message reaches Notion. The subject, snippet,
body, Gmail message id and sender address are read to find those two
values and are then discarded inside **Parse Notification**, so no
later node can write them.

When no display name can be read, the row is named
`HubSpot Community participant` rather than falling back to the
subject line. The `Signal` text is a fixed phrase, not a quote from
the mail.

## Configure before running

1. Open **Scout Setup** and paste your Notion database id.
2. Bind a Gmail OAuth2 credential on **Community Notifications** and a
   Notion credential on **Find Existing Row** and **Write to Notion**.

**Validate Setup** stops the run before the first Notion request while
the database id is still empty, and names the field to fix.
